# Review — PAN-5452
## Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — `--no-screenshot` is silently ignored on every action and `get-app-state` (Commander stores it as `screenshot: false`, the library reads `noScreenshot`)

## Context
- Run ID: agent-pan-5452-review-01a05af0
- Manifest: /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-5452/.pan/review/agent-pan-5452-review-01a05af0/context.json
- Branch / workspace: feature/pan-5452 / /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-5452
- PR: https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/pull/5457
- HEAD reviewed: 01a05af009b696ff230949d3740bfcee77e4b1b4
- Base / prior cycle SHA: origin/main; no prior review cycle
- Acceptance criteria source: the manifest's `acceptanceCriteria` list is empty, so AC-1 to AC-9 come from `.pan/drafts/pan-5452.md`.

## Blocking Findings

### [correctness] `--no-screenshot` never reaches the helper — `src/cli/commands/computer.ts:31`
- Severity: ! (MUST)
- Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect; in_pr_scope.
- Trigger and changed-code connection: `addActionOptions` declares `.option('--no-screenshot', …)`. Commander treats a `--no-<x>` flag as the negation of `x`, so the parsed options carry `screenshot: false` (default `true`), never `noScreenshot`. Each action handler passes `options` straight to the library (`getAppState(options)`, `click(options)`, …). `baseFields()` in `src/lib/computer-use/commands.ts:42-48` reads only `options.noScreenshot`, which is always `undefined`. So the operation never carries `noScreenshot: true`. This affects `get-app-state` and all ten action commands, because every one of them goes through `baseFields`.
- Expected / observed / impact: Expected: PRD WI-3c field table (`--no-screenshot` → `noScreenshot: true`) and WI-4 item 1 ("Every action and `get-app-state` take … `--no-screenshot`"). The docs (`configuration/computer-use.mdx:45`), the skill (`SKILL.md:112`, `:133`) and the generated composer manifest all advertise the flag. Observed: the flag is accepted and has no effect. Impact: every call captures the window, writes a PNG under `~/.overdeck/computer-use/screenshots/`, and moves up to 64 MB of base64 through the helper pipe, even when the agent or operator asked for no pixels (for example to avoid saving sensitive window content to disk). Nothing else breaks. `wait` is unaffected because it sets `noScreenshot: true` itself.
- Evidence: a runtime reproduction. A temporary vitest probe registered `registerComputerCommands` on a fresh `Command`, mocked `commands.js`, and parsed `computer get-app-state --app calc --no-screenshot`. `getAppState` received `{ screenshot: false, app: 'calc' }`, and the assertion `toMatchObject({ noScreenshot: true })` failed. The probe file was deleted afterwards and the tree is clean apart from a pipeline-written `.pan/continues` update. Limitation: not reproduced against the live helper, but the operation object never contains the field, so the helper's `include_screenshot = not bool(operation.get("noScreenshot"))` is always true.
- Fix: in `computer.ts`, map `screenshot === false` to `noScreenshot: true` before calling the library. Either do this in a small adapter used by every action handler, or change `BaseAppOptions` to accept `screenshot?: boolean` and have `baseFields` set `noScreenshot` when `screenshot === false`. Add a CLI test case in `tests/unit/cli/computer-command.test.ts` that asserts `--no-screenshot` produces `noScreenshot: true` (or the equivalent) on the mocked call (see the validation gap below).

### [validation] No test covers the CLI → library flag wiring for `--no-screenshot` — `tests/unit/cli/computer-command.test.ts:1`
- Severity: ~ (SHOULD; it travels with the blocker above)
- Classification / requirement scope: validation gap; in_pr_scope.
- Trigger and changed-code connection: `computer-command.test.ts` mocks `commands.js` and checks only `click --element-index/--click-count`. `commands.test.ts` calls the library with `noScreenshot: true` directly. So no test crosses the Commander boundary for the negated flag, and the defect above passed 131 green tests.
- Fix: add the CLI assertion described above.

## Non-blocking Findings

1. **~ [correctness] An empty or corrupt `lease.json` blocks every input command and `release --force` — `src/lib/computer-use/lease.ts:60-67`.** This is an implementation defect, in_pr_scope. `readLease` rethrows any error other than ENOENT, and both `claimLease` and `releaseLease` call it before they check `force`. I reproduced it with `npx tsx` against a scratch `OVERDECK_HOME` holding a zero-byte `lease.json`. `claimLease` threw `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input`, and so did `releaseLease({ force: true })`. The CLI then reports this as `helper_error`. This contradicts the PRD statement that `release` exists "so an operator can always clear a stuck lease". A crash mid-write can leave a zero-byte file: this machine has a recorded history of crash-reboot zero-byte truncation, and the lease write is a plain `writeFile`, not an atomic rename. Recovery today is a manual `rm` of the file. Fix: treat an unparseable lease as absent (or as expired), at least on the `force` path, and add a lease test for it.
2. **~ [requirements/docs] The PR body says the screenshot-geometry anomaly is "already covered by this PR's docs ('Limits'…)", but it isn't.** `configuration/computer-use.mdx` "Limits" and `SKILL.md` say nothing about occluded or wrong-window screenshots or about wrong window bounds. A grep for `occlu|wrong window|geometry|multi-monitor` found nothing. This is a documentation gap, in_pr_scope. Fix: add a Limits bullet (and a skill note) saying that, on some apps or multi-monitor setups, AT-SPI can report window bounds at `(0,0)`. In that case screenshots can show the wrong area and coordinate input can miss. Agents should verify with the accessibility tree and prefer element (AT-SPI action) clicks.
3. **? [security/safety] Synthetic pointer input may aim at the wrong screen area on the same geometry bug.** This is an unconfirmed hypothesis about upstream behaviour, and pre_existing in the vendored helper. In `runtime.py`, `screen_point` (line 1372) computes coordinate clicks, scroll and drag as `window_rect.x + x`, with `window_rect = screen_rect(window)`. Element points come from `screen_rect(node)`, using the same `Atspi.CoordType.SCREEN` extents. Live verification recorded `(0,0,360,491)` for gnome-calculator while X11 placed it at `(3829,536)`. If element extents share that offset, a synthetic click, scroll or drag would land on whatever sits near the screen origin, which could be another app. Live verification exercised only the AT-SPI action click path. What would establish it: a coordinate `click` on a GTK4 app on the secondary monitor in a throwaway session, watching where the pointer lands. The remedy cannot be an edit to `runtime.py` (non-goal 5). It would be docs or a TypeScript-side guard (for example, refusing coordinate input when the window rect origin is `(0,0)` but `list_windows` disagrees), or an upstream fix plus re-vendor.
4. **~ [correctness] `--max-elements` does nothing without `--query`.** `applyTreeFilter` (`commands.ts:108`) applies `maxElements` only inside `filterTree`. The CLI help says so ("Cap the number of matching lines kept by --query"), but `SKILL.md:47` says "`--max-elements <n>` caps how many elements are printed", which reads as standalone. Fix: align the skill wording, or reject `--max-elements` without `--query` with `invalid_argument`.
5. **? [spec] `mentionsMissingAtspi` can misclassify runtime errors.** `helper.ts:54` maps any `ok:false` message matching `/\bgi\b/` or `/atspi/i` to `helper_missing_dependency`, with the apt fix replacing the real message. An AT-SPI D-Bus runtime error string (for example one naming `org.a11y.atspi`) would then lose its real text. This follows PRD 3c literally, so it's a specification defect, not an implementation one. A narrower match (`ModuleNotFoundError`, `PyGObject unavailable`, `Namespace Atspi not available`) would be safer.
6. **? [correctness] `maxBuffer` overflow reports as `helper_timeout`.** When stdout exceeds 64 MB, Node kills the child and sets `killed: true`, so `isTimeoutError` reports a timeout. This is unlikely given the screenshot sizes, and the impact is only the wording of the message.
7. **? [UX] The `pan doctor` row can go silent.** With the feature on, if every probe passes but the helper `handshake` fails for a reason other than `gi`, `checkComputerUse` returns no rows at all, so the operator gets neither `Ready` nor a cause. The `gsettings` probe also runs with the shell's env rather than the resolved desktop env, so it can report accessibility off from an agent shell that has no session bus. Suggest an `error` row carrying the handshake's message when it fails.
8. **? [UX] The subtree note isn't the last line.** PRD 3e says the note should be "the command output's last line". `applyTreeFilter` appends it to `treeLines`, so the text output prints `Focused:` and `Screenshot:` after it. This is cosmetic.

### Dimensions
- **Correctness:** I traced the preamble order (platform → config → env → lock → lease → helper → cache and screenshot under the same lock), the read-versus-input lease rule, the wait loop's per-poll locking and `appNotFound` retry, and helper error mapping (`killed` timeout, ENOENT, last-line JSON parse, `ok:false`). Snapshot cache semantics (subtree replacement) match PRD 3e. The blocker is in the CLI flag mapping; item 1 is the lease robustness gap.
- **Security:** D-3 holds end to end. Every project-YAML path goes through `stripProjectSecurity`: `load.ts` lines 104/112 (sync) and 157/164 (async). The remaining `mergeConfigs` callers (`model-presets/apply.ts:161`, `settings-api.ts:644`) never read a project `.pan.yaml`. Op files are written at mode 0600 in a 0700 dir and removed in `finally`. `execFile` is used with an argv array, so there is no shell injection. The stdin flags keep secrets out of argv. The blocked-shortcut port matches Orca's `LINUX_RULES` and `findBlockedKeyCombo` (the diff shows formatting only). Per the threat model, holder-id impersonation by trusted local agents is out of scope. Items 3 and 5 are recorded as hypotheses.
- **Performance:** every call is async (`execFile` through promises, `fs/promises`); there is no `execSync`, `spawnSync` or `/tmp/` in the new code (grep is empty). Lock waiting is bounded (15 ms retry, about 60 s cap, 60 s stale reclaim, 30 s helper timeout with SIGKILL). Screenshot pruning is bounded at 50 files. The blocker adds an avoidable screenshot capture per call when the operator opts out.
